name: lua-l1-declaration-evaluator
title: Lua edit-host option B, PR L1: declarations-only evaluator (throwaway budgeted state, no engine bindings) that reads a script's field declarations without running script code
issue: Design (APPROVED by the user 2026-10-15, option B): C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/security-design-lua-editmode-and-preauth-slots.md PART 1 (read 1.1-1.9 FULLY first: what runs today and when, what the editor needs from a script in edit mode, option B 'declaration-only evaluation in a throwaway, budgeted state with no engine bindings', 1.4 recommendation, 1.5 migration, 1.6 tests, 1.7 staged PR plan, 1.8 decisions, 1.9 risks) and the audit finding F3b in C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/editor-host-security-audit-2026-10-15.md. Decisions: edit-host Lua = option B (declarations-only evaluation in a throwaway state with 1M instruction / 16 MiB budgets and NO engine bindings; OnDisable/OnDestroy stop running on the edit host; no opt-in flag). MERGED prerequisites: sec-lua-budget #159 (budgets, sandbox prelude, LuaBudgetScope, panic repair, RunChunk) and sec-lua-registry-reserve #173 (reserve-then-copy; DescribeFields reads SerializableFields via the Lua C API into plain data): read both PRs' docs/scripting-lua.html sections first and REUSE their machinery (do not duplicate the budget/panic logic). This item is ONLY 'PR L1': build the DECLARATION EVALUATOR as a library component that is NOT wired into the editor host yet (wiring, the single scene build, the Quit guard and docs are L2): an API like `Scripting::DeclarationEvaluator::Evaluate(sourceOrPath) -> DeclarationResult { fields (name, type, default, attributes as DescribeFields returns today), errors, budgetExceeded }` that (1) creates a THROWAWAY lua_State (own allocator with a 16 MiB cap, instruction budget 1M via the same hook mechanism but its own LuaBudgetScope, sandboxed libraries exactly like the engine sandbox minus ALL engine bindings: no Application/GameObject/Input/etc, no io/os/require of engine modules; `require` of project modules either refused or resolved to ANOTHER declaration evaluation (decide per design 1.4/1.5 and record as a deviation), (2) runs the chunk (class definition code) so `SerializableFields`/declarations tables are built, reads them via the C API into plain data (reuse DescribeFields' reading logic), (3) closes the state: nothing persists, no engine object is touched, (4) reports script errors and budget/memory exhaustion as data, never crashing; scripts that call engine bindings during evaluation (e.g. top-level `Debug.Log(...)`, `GameObject.Find(...)`) must NOT fail the declaration read: bindings are absent so such calls raise 'attempt to index a nil value'; the evaluator must be tolerant: provide a minimal inert stub table for the commonly used global names listed in the design (find them in the design/1.5 migration: e.g. engine globals resolve to a callable-inert proxy that returns itself, so top-level engine calls do not abort the class definition) and document exactly which behaviours differ from a real run (declarations that depend on engine state computed at load time are not representable: the field list must then be reported as 'unevaluable' with the reason, not silently empty). Tests (all legs; web too if Lua tests run there): well-formed script yields the same fields as today's DescribeFields for the project's real scripts (use lua_project scripts and the existing test scripts as a corpus: compare the evaluator's result to the current runtime path field by field), infinite loop at top level => budgetExceeded in bounded time, memory bomb => memory exhausted not crash, top-level engine call tolerated via inert stubs, script that errors => error as data, no engine singleton touched (LuaRuntime::Instance not created/used), evaluator usable concurrently from several threads (independent states) if the design requires it, nothing leaks (state closed on every path: use the allocator counters). Docs: a section in docs/scripting-lua.html for the evaluator API and its limits ONLY (L2 documents the editor behaviour change). Nothing builds locally; CI (10 checks) is the test. Unverified items: wasm/MSVC-Debug specifics of the error paths (the known-limitation notes in docs/scripting-lua.html apply: do not rely on error text read off the stack; use runtime state), anything wiring-related.
acceptance: A DeclarationEvaluator library API exists, not wired into the editor host
Throwaway budgeted state (1M instructions, 16 MiB), sandboxed, no engine bindings, closed on every path; errors/budget/memory reported as data
Output matches today's DescribeFields on the repo's real scripts (corpus test); top-level engine calls tolerated via inert stubs and unevaluable cases reported explicitly
All 10 checks green; docs describe the API and its limits
notes: Reviewer: sandbox completeness (no engine binding or global reachable, no io/os/debug/package, string metatable etc), budget/memory enforcement actually applies to the throwaway state (not the main runtime's LuaBudgetScope state), no shared static state with LuaRuntime (thread safety, seeds from determinism.luaSeed still applied or irrelevant), the inert-stub proxy cannot be used to escape or to hang (infinite loops through stub calls are budgeted), corpus equality test is meaningful, nothing leaks, docs true. Unverified: L2 wiring.
